newsitem.title: USA: Florida sees August trial start in tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: Florida sees August trial start in tobacco case.

text.p: Florida sees as near certain an August 4 start in the high-profile trial on the state government's $1 billion lawsuit against tobacco companies, now that the U.S. Supreme Court has rejected a constitutional challenge.
"It removes a possible hurdle to going to trial on August 4," Dexter Douglas, general counsel to Gov. Lawton Chiles, said in an interview.

The U.S. Supreme Court in Washington on Monday let stand a Florida Supreme Court ruling that the state government has the legal right under a 1994 state law to sue cigarette makers for Medicaid costs incurred by Florida from tobacco-related illnesses.
The Florida suit is one of 22 such legal actions filed by state governments throughout the United States. A trial in the suit brought by Mississippi's attorney general is due to begin in June.
"We're very pleased," Douglass said of the U.S. Supreme court action.
Douglass said the defendants, which include Philip Morris Cos Inc and the Brown & Williamson unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, had few other apparent moves left to put off an August 4 trial start.
"The judge has been very aggressive in making sure we all stick to schedule," Douglass said.

Trial Judge Harold Cohen of Palm Beach County Court has repeatedly said during pre-trial hearings that he was aiming for an August 4 trial start. Lawyers on both sides estimate the trial will last several months.

Cohen last month rejected a request from tobacco company lawyers that the state trial be postponed until completion of a class-action suit in Miami on behalf of all sick cigarette smokers or their survivors in Florida. That trial is scheduled to begin in early June and expected to last for several months.
